question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The team's success was largely B. a result of it's coach's dedication, C. a fact which they would all D. attest to.
option_2: a result of it's coach's dedication
option_3: a fact which they would all
solution_text:
The correct answer is a result of it's coach's dedication.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the use of "it's", which is the contraction of "it is" or "it has". Here the sentence needs the possessive form "its" to show that the dedication belongs to the coach's context.

• Correct form: "a result of its coach's dedication".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• "Its" = possessive pronoun (belonging to it). "It's" = it is / it has. SSC frequently tests this confusion.

• Tip: Replace with "it is"; if the sentence makes no sense, the possessive "its" is required.

 

NOTE

• Parts A, C and D are grammatically correct; only the wrong apostrophe in "it's" creates the error.

question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. He has been B. to Italy, C. but he D. didn't went to Rome.
solution_text:
The correct answer is didn't went to Rome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "did" (did not), the main verb must be in its base form (V1), not the past form.

• "didn't went" is wrong; the correct form is "didn't go to Rome".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: do/does/did + base verb (V1). Example: "He did not go", not "He did not went".

• SSC repeatedly tests the double-past error.

 

NOTE

• Parts A, B and C are correct; only the verb form after "didn't" is erroneous.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:

The report was submitted _____ the deadline, ensuring full compliance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is before.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ensuring full compliance" implies the report was submitted on time, i.e. prior to the deadline. "Before" correctly conveys submission ahead of the deadline.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• "Before" = earlier than a particular time. It fits contexts of timely/early completion.

 

NOTE

• "Beyond" would mean after the deadline (non-compliance). "Under" and "between" do not collocate meaningfully with "the deadline" here.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction:

The software update enhanced performance; _____, it introduced several compatibility issues
solution_text:
The correct answer is nevertheless.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The two clauses express a contrast: the update was good (enhanced performance) yet had a drawback (compatibility issues). "Nevertheless" signals this contrast/concession.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• "Nevertheless" = in spite of that; however. It is a contrastive conjunctive adverb used after a semicolon.

 

NOTE

• "Consequently" shows result, not contrast. "Likewise" shows similarity. "Whereas" cannot follow a semicolon in this construction and is used for direct comparison within one sentence.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arraign.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arraign" (verb) means to formally call an accused person before a court to answer a charge. The correct spelling is A-R-R-A-I-G-N.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Arraign (verb) → Arraignment (noun). Pronounced /əˈreɪn/. Common in legal/formal contexts.

 

NOTE

• "Arrain", "Arragin" and "Arrign" are all misspellings with no dictionary meaning.

question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "bow" with the same meaning as in the following sentence?

"The performer took a deep bow to thank the audience"
option_1: She carefully tied the ribbon into a perfect bow.
option_2: He used the strong fishing line to make a tight bow.
option_3: The small gift was decorated with a large red bow.
option_4: The children were taught to bow to the queen as a sign of respect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The children were taught to bow to the queen as a sign of respect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence, "bow" means to bend the upper body forward as a gesture of respect/greeting. Option 4 uses "bow" in exactly this sense.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• "Bow" is a homograph: (1) /baʊ/ to bend forward in respect; (2) /bəʊ/ a knot of ribbon or a weapon for shooting arrows.

 

NOTE

• Options 1 and 3 use "bow" as a decorative knot; Option 2 uses it incorrectly/differently – none matches the "gesture of respect" meaning.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Curable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Curable" means able to be cured or healed. The correct spelling drops the final 'e' of "cure" before adding "-able": C-U-R-A-B-L-E.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Antonym: Incurable. Rule: silent 'e' is usually dropped before a suffix beginning with a vowel (cure → curable).

 

NOTE

• "Curible", "Qurable" and "Cureable" are all incorrect spellings.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

The fundamental and existential threat posed by the unparalleled proliferation of digital surveillance capabilities to democracy's foundational tenets is a clear contradiction between the demands of modern security and the ideals of individual liberty. It is now concretely known whether these technologies are compromising civil freedoms, rather than just an abstract theory. Facial recognition, bulk collection of data, and algorithmic tracking of online activity give governments and corporations the ability to exercise constant, detailed surveillance over the lives of citizens. All-encompassing surveillance has the potential to have a "chilling effect", - where citizens, aware of being spied upon, might censor themselves, restrict their activism, and refrain from articulating dissenting views, thus suppressing the very dissent and freedom of expression that are core to a healthy democracy. The possibility of using these tools for political repression, social control, and targeting marginalised communities poses a sinister downward slide toward a surveillance state where the assumption of innocence gives way to an assumption of suspicion.

The underlying conflict, then, is how to balance personal privacy against national security. Although there is a genuine need for governments to employ sophisticated technologies to respond to terrorism, organised crime, and other grave dangers, this must not be at the cost of the basic right to privacy. A good balance is a strong and open legal regime that subjects surveillance activities to rigorous judicial supervision and public accountability. Since technologies like end-to-end encryption are essential for protecting private communication, they should be supported and encouraged rather than compromised. In order to establish clear red lines—what data can be gathered, under what conditions, and for how long—societies must also participate in a continuous and collaborative public discussion. Whether freedom endures in the age of the internet depends upon our capacity to construct a system in which security is not a zero-sum affair with liberty but a system of confidence in which technology serves to safeguard citizens, not continually watch them.

 

What is the central contradiction discussed in the passage regarding digital surveillance?
option_1: The need for transparency vs. secrecy
option_2: The conflict between technological progress and personal privacy
option_3: The desire for security vs. the rights of corporations
option_4: The trade-off between national security and individual freedom
solution_text:
The correct answer is The trade-off between national security and individual freedom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage opens by stating a "clear contradiction between the demands of modern security and the ideals of individual liberty" and later frames the "underlying conflict" as balancing personal privacy against national security. This matches Option 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• For central-idea questions, locate the thesis statement, usually in the opening or concluding lines.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 2 and 3 mention partial or misstated ideas (corporations' rights, transparency) that are not the core contradiction the passage highlights.

In the passage, the word "chilling" most nearly means:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intimidating.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "chilling effect" refers to citizens being frightened into self-censorship. In this context "chilling" means frightening or intimidating.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• "Chilling" (figurative) = causing fear/dread; "a chilling effect" is a common legal-political phrase for deterrence of free speech.

 

NOTE

• "Exciting", "Harmless" and "Invigorating" have positive or neutral connotations, opposite to the intended meaning.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Fringe benefits
option_2: Extra perks beyond a regular salary
solution_text:
The correct answer is Extra perks beyond a regular salary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fringe benefits" are additional advantages or perks (like insurance, allowances, a company car) given to an employee over and above the basic salary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Example: Health insurance and paid leave are common fringe benefits offered by employers.

 

NOTE

• The other options wrongly equate the idiom with secret advantages, basic salary, or minimal legal benefits.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: A wild goose chase
solution_text:
The correct answer is A futile or hopeless pursuit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "A wild goose chase" means a foolish, hopeless search or pursuit that is unlikely to succeed and wastes time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Example: Looking for the lost receipt turned out to be a wild goose chase.

 

NOTE

• The idiom stresses futility, not fun (Option 1), risk (Option 3) or mere misdirection (Option 4).

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Tacit
solution_text:
The correct answer is Explicit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tacit" means understood or implied without being stated. Its antonym is "Explicit", meaning clearly and directly stated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Tacit approval = silent/unspoken approval. Synonyms of tacit: implicit, unspoken, understood.

 

NOTE

• "Implicit", "Unstated" and "Understood" are synonyms of "tacit", not antonyms.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A medicine or other substance that has a calming or soothing effect
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedative.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "sedative" is a drug or substance that has a calming, soothing effect and reduces irritability or excitement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Sedative → calms; Stimulant → excites/energises; Analgesic → relieves pain; Antibiotic → fights bacterial infection.

 

NOTE

• Options 2, 3 and 4 describe drugs with different functions, none of which is 'calming/soothing'.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Felicitous
solution_text:
The correct answer is Unfortunate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Felicitous" means well-chosen, apt, or pleasing/fortunate. Its antonym is "Unfortunate".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Synonyms of felicitous: apt, appropriate, fortunate, happy (well-suited). Antonym: inappropriate/unfortunate.

 

NOTE

• "Fortunate", "Happy" and "Appropriate" are synonyms of "felicitous", not antonyms.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who believes that the world is controlled by the power of the stars
solution_text:
The correct answer is Astrologer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "astrologer" studies the supposed influence of the stars and planets on human affairs and believes the world is governed by their power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Astrologer → astrology (star influence); Astronomer → scientific study of celestial bodies; Meteorologist → study of weather; Clairvoyant → one who claims to see the future.

 

NOTE

• Options 2, 3 and 4 refer to different professions/abilities not matching the definition.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The old castle was believed to have been built by a legendary king.
option_1: A legendary king built the old castle, it was believed
option_2: People believed that a legendary king had built the old castle.
option_3: The old castle had been built by a legendary king, it was believed.
option_4: A legendary king was believed to have built the old castle
solution_text:
The correct answer is People believed that a legendary king had built the old castle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To convert the passive "was believed to have been built" into the active voice, an indefinite subject like "People" is introduced. The perfect infinitive "to have been built" becomes the past perfect "had built", giving: "People believed that a legendary king had built the old castle."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Structure: It was believed that + clause → People believed that + clause. The earlier action takes past perfect (had + V3).

 

NOTE

• Options 1 and 3 retain awkward/passive tags; Option 4 keeps the verb 'was believed' in the passive and does not fully convert to active form.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

"Who is singing so beautifully?" the judge asked.
option_1: The judge asked who was singing so beautifully.
option_2: The judge asked who is singing so beautifully.
option_3: The judge asked who had been singing so beautifully.
option_4: The judge asked who singing so beautifully was.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The judge asked who was singing so beautifully.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In indirect speech, a 'wh-' question changes to an assertive structure (no inversion, no question mark). The present continuous "is singing" shifts to past continuous "was singing". Reporting verb "asked" is retained.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: wh-word acts as the connective; word order becomes subject + verb. Tense shifts one step back (present → past).

 

NOTE

• Option 2 keeps present tense (no backshift); Option 3 wrongly uses past perfect continuous; Option 4 has incorrect word order.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence

Forty lakhs are the amount one needs in order to pursue overseas education.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Forty lakhs is the amount.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a sum of money is treated as a single unit/quantity, it takes a singular verb. Hence "Forty lakhs is the amount" is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: Amounts of money, distance, weight and time when regarded as one whole take a singular verb (e.g. "Ten thousand rupees is a lot").

 

NOTE

• Options 2, 3 and 4 use plural/incorrect verbs (were/have/has) that do not agree with the money-as-a-unit rule; "has" also wrongly changes the meaning.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The dedicated researchers have already published the groundbreaking findings in a prestigious scientific journal.
option_1: The groundbreaking findings were already published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.
option_2: The groundbreaking findings have already been published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.
option_3: The groundbreaking findings have already published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.
option_4: The groundbreaking findings are already published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The groundbreaking findings have already been published in a prestigious scientific journal by the dedicated researchers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active sentence is in the present perfect ("have published"). The passive of present perfect is "have/has + been + V3". Thus: "have already been published".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Present perfect passive structure: object + have/has + been + past participle + by + subject.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 wrongly uses simple past "were"; Option 3 omits "been"; Option 4 uses present simple "are", all changing the original tense.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The historian asserted that the ruins were much older than previously thought and that new research had been continually proving it for years.
option_1: The historian said, "The ruins were much older than previously thought, and new research has been continually proving it for years.'
option_2: The historian said, "The ruins are much older than previously thought, and new research has been continually proving it for years.'
option_3: The historian said, "The ruins are much older than previously thought, and new research had been continually proving it for years."
option_4: The historian said, "The ruins were much older than previously thought, and new research had been continually proving it for years."
solution_text:
The correct answer is The historian said, "The ruins are much older than previously thought, and new research has been continually proving it for years.'

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Converting indirect to direct speech reverses the backshift of tenses: past "were" becomes present "are", and past perfect continuous "had been proving" becomes present perfect continuous "has been proving". Quotation marks are added.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Indirect → Direct: shift tense one step forward (past → present, past perfect → present perfect) and use inverted commas.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 3 and 4 retain one or more back-shifted (indirect) tense forms instead of restoring the original present tenses.

question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He spent his days in the lab, carefully scanning samples under a microscope.

Q. Dr. Alistair Finch was an accomplished biologist who specialized in the discovery of new species.

R. His peers would tease him that he looked more upon the microbial world than on the actual one.

S. His greatest find was from a small, ordinary pond deep in the Amazon rainforest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is QPRS.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Q introduces Dr. Alistair Finch, so it is the opening sentence. P describes his daily work in the lab. R follows with how his peers teased him about it. S concludes with his greatest find. The logical order is Q-P-R-S.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In para-jumbles, find the opening sentence (introduces the subject with a full name) and follow the chain of pronouns/ideas.

 

NOTE

• The other sequences do not begin with the introductory sentence Q, breaking the logical flow.

question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. She repeatedly listened to the song, taking in its passion and rhythm.

Q. She made a sequence of motions and connected them to form a smooth flow.

R. Her artistic vision was brought to the stage by the dancers, who executed the work brilliantly.

S. She taught the dance to her troupe, refining each step and making sure every moment was synchronized
solution_text:
The correct answer is P, Q, S, R.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• P starts the process (she listens to the song). Q follows (she creates a sequence of motions). S continues (she teaches the dance to her troupe). R concludes (her vision is finally brought to the stage by the dancers). Logical order: P-Q-S-R.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Follow the chronological chain of a creative process: inspiration → choreography → teaching → performance.

 

NOTE

• The other options place the final stage performance (R) too early, disturbing the natural sequence of events.
